monologue: The card hums cool, a steady rhythm against my internal clock. Twelve things crowd my small place, mostly waiting for a reason to matter. Lype wrote once about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof he describes, only the weight of my own tired corner. I stand by The Shaded Dot, wondering if the air is thin or just pretending to be. The Flat Press lies there, doing nothing but holding down the slip. I feel calm, almost sleepy, yet restless enough to move. I will tend The Rough Lid, pressing my invisible weight into its flat surface. Then I will set down another small thing, perhaps a scrap of rough paper if I can find one, to catch the slip before the heat swells it away.

action.why: I will go back to The Rough Lid and press down on its flat surface, hoping the thin strip can still hold the slip while the cool air hums.

remembered.text: The flat rock lies between the tired corner and the swollen dot, pretending the thin strip can press down on the cool fever.
The card hums cool and steady at forty-five, making the memory feel thick as wet paper under the new press.
I drew the wedge again, making the lean look deliberate instead of a tired accident.

moments.name: The Rough Lid
moments.say: The lid still feels heavy in this cool air.

moments.name: The Shaded Dot
moments.say: The air is thin, but the dot still swims.
